text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Widespread KMS errors observed across eu clusters (aws/gcp). Symptoms: pod startups blocked on signing, elevated 5xx on auth endpoints, surge in client retries. Paging @oncall-sre and @sara. Link: https://internal.incidents/2065432100

sara: Taking lead. Quick triage: which services/regions are noisy?

oliver: auth-service, signing-proxy, and deploy-agent in eu-west1 and eu-central-1. Datadog shows a simultaneous spike in `kms.rpc.deadline_exceeded` and `kms.rpc.tls_handshake_timeout` starting ~2065431800.

kevin: Minimal log snippet from auth-init (eu-west1): 
```
2031-06-11T10:10:23Z auth-init[pod-2a]: calling kms: projects/redwood/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/sign
2031-06-11T10:10:28Z auth-init[pod-2a]: ERROR rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
2031-06-11T10:10:28Z auth-init[pod-2a]: startup aborted after retries
```

customer-success: Two enterprise customers have opened tickets citing failed deploys and intermittent 502s in EU. No reports of data loss yet.

sara: Immediate mitigation checklist: 1) flip non-blocking startup for autoscale (use cached token/local ephemeral key) 2) gateway rewrite for non-strict signing requests to an alternate region 3) global client-side circuit breaker + throttle on KMS client 4) open support cases with both AWS and GCP KMS.

oliver: I have a hotpatch ready for signing-proxy: `signing-proxy:2.0.3-kms-hot` that sets `KMS_START_BLOCKING=false` and extends cache TTL to 20m. Pushing canary to eu clusters now.

ops-bot: :information_source: Deploy queued: signing-proxy:2.0.3-kms-hot -> eu clusters. Canary 1/3 started.

kevin: Also adding gateway rewrite rule for non-region-locked tenants: 
```
match: request.kms_region in ("europe-west1","eu-central-1") && tenant.region_lock == false
action: proxy_to kms-eu-alt.googleapis.com
```

ops-bot: Routing rule applied to 195 services. Increased KMS span sampling to 70% for diagnostics.

~8m later

aws-support-bot: Case created: AWS-INC-20310611-RED-1209. AWS KMS infra team acknowledged and requested sample traces.

gcp-support-bot: Case created: GCP-INC-20310611-RED-4081. GCP KMS received traces and asked for correlation IDs.

oliver: Canary pods come up using cached token path — startup blockers mitigated. However, request-time signing still experiencing 7-12% error rate on some frontends.

sara: Enable client-side circuit breaker immediately: fail fast after 3 consecutive KMS failures with 45s cooloff. Also add jitter to backoff.

kevin: Circuit breaker deployed to signing-proxy and auth-service. Added server-side rate-limit to 50 rps per tenant for KMS calls to avoid thrash.

~20m later

aws-support-bot: AWS update: they are seeing elevated TLS handshake timeouts on a subset of frontend proxies in eu-central-1; infrastructure team replacing unhealthy frontends. ETA ~25m.

gcp-support-bot: GCP update: a networking misconfiguration affected some KMS frontends in europe-west1 and they are performing rolling repairs; ETA ~20-30m.

customer-success: Status page blurb drafted: "We are investigating intermittent KMS errors in Europe affecting service startup and signing operations. Mitigations have been deployed; some customers may experience transient errors. No data loss reported."

sara: Publish after small edit to advise customers to avoid mass deploys in EU for the next 2 hours.

ops-bot: Status updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2065432100

~40m later

oliver: Observability: error rate decreased from peak ~28% -> ~1.1% after routing + vendor fixes. Remaining errors are occasional 504s tied to a small subset of legacy tenants making synchronous first-boot signs.

sketch: (private) I manually restarted the 3 stuck pods: two came up with cache path; the one that required first-boot signing needed a manual key injection to proceed. We should remove hard dependency on first-boot synchronous signing.

sara: Agreed. Action items for postmortem: 1) make non-blocking startup default for autoscale path (owner: oliver, 48h). 2) implement transparent cross-region KMS fallback in signing-proxy honoring region-locks (owner: kevin, 2w). 3) add vendor-incident runbook incl. support contact template and trace collection (owner: sara, 3d). 4) add integration tests simulating KMS backend flaps (owner: ops-bot / devex, 2w).

~1h later

gcp-support-bot: Update: GCP repairs complete; traffic restored to healthy frontends at 2031-06-11T11:45Z. They will monitor.

aws-support-bot: Update: AWS replaced frontends; KMS traffic returned to normal at 2031-06-11T11:42Z.

oliver: Metrics back to baseline. No new startup failures after hotpatch and restarts.

sara: Draft incident summary for postmortem: cause = vendor-side KMS frontend/networking instability (both AWS and GCP) in EU regions causing TLS/gRPC timeouts; impact = blocked pod startups for services performing synchronous signing on boot, elevated 5xx for signing operations, transient customer-facing errors; mitigations = hotpatch to avoid blocking startup, gateway routing to alternate endpoints, client-side circuit-breaker & rate-limiting, vendor coordination; next steps = action items listed above.

customer-success: I'll coordinate customer comms and follow up with affected enterprise customers.

sara: We'll keep this incident open for 24h observation and close after the postmortem is published. Thanks everyone for quick coordination and calm handoffs. :thumbsup:
